description: All eight domain enums expose exactly the member names specified in the BRD data model
steps: Import Role, CustomerStatus, KycStatus, AccountStatus, TransactionDirection, TransferStatus, LoanStatus and NotificationStatus from backend.src.types
Assert set(Role) member values equal {'CUSTOMER','ADMIN'}
Assert set(LoanStatus) member values equal {'APPLIED','UNDER_REVIEW','APPROVED','REJECTED','DISBURSED'}
Assert every enum member is a str subclass so it serialises to JSON as its value

description: Every domain exception subclasses DomainError and exposes a distinct non-empty error_code
steps: Import DomainError and its seven named subclasses from backend.src.types
Assert each subclass is a subclass of DomainError
Assert InsufficientFundsException().error_code == 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS'
Assert the set of error_code values across all subclasses has no duplicates and none is empty

description: No exception type exists for a withdrawn rule such as a transfer cap or beneficiary precondition
steps: Run: grep -rniE 'DailyTransferCap|CapExceeded|NotBeneficiary|Eligibility.*Error' backend/src/types/
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Enumerate all DomainError subclasses and assert none relates to a transfer cap, velocity limit or beneficiary requirement

description: The types package has zero outbound imports to any higher layer
steps: Run: grep -rnE 'from (backend\.)?src\.(config|repository|service|api)|import (backend\.)?src\.(config|repository|service|api)' backend/src/types/
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches found)
Import backend.src.types in a fresh interpreter and assert no ImportError is raised

description: The types package passes mypy in strict mode with zero errors
steps: Run: cd backend && uv run mypy --strict src/types/
Assert the process exit code is 0
Assert stdout contains 'Success' and does not contain 'error:'

description: The JWT signing key is environment-sourced with no hard-coded fallback
steps: Run: grep -rniE 'secret[_-]?key\s*[:=]\s*["'\''][A-Za-z0-9]' backend/src/config/
Assert the command produces no output (no literal key assigned in source)
Unset JWT_SECRET_KEY and instantiate Settings inside pytest.raises for a validation error
Assert the error is raised and no default key is used

description: JWT expiry and database URL are typed settings overridable from the environment
steps: Instantiate Settings with JWT_SECRET_KEY set and assert jwt_expiry_minutes is a positive int
Set JWT_EXPIRY_MINUTES='15' and reload Settings
Assert settings.jwt_expiry_minutes == 15
Set DATABASE_URL to a temporary path, reload, and assert settings.database_url reflects it

description: The default statement page size is a configurable setting, not a service-layer literal
steps: Instantiate Settings and assert statement_page_size is a positive int
Override STATEMENT_PAGE_SIZE='5' in the environment and reload Settings
Assert settings.statement_page_size == 5
Run: grep -rnE 'page_size\s*=\s*[0-9]+' backend/src/service/ and assert no hard-coded default is found

description: No invented transfer cap or loan eligibility threshold exists in configuration
steps: Run: grep -rniE 'daily_cap|transfer_cap|velocity|max_principal|min_principal|income_ratio|max_tenure' backend/src/config/
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Introspect the Settings model field names and assert none contains 'cap' or 'eligib'

description: Config layer imports no layer above Types and typechecks strictly
steps: Run: grep -rnE 'from (backend\.)?src\.(repository|service|api)' backend/src/config/
Assert the command exits with status 1
Run: cd backend && uv run mypy --strict src/config/ and assert exit code 0

description: A .env.example documents required variables and contains no real secret values
steps: Assert backend/.env.example exists and contains JWT_SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL
Assert .env is listed in .gitignore
Assert no value in .env.example matches a high-entropy secret pattern

description: parse_money returns an exact Decimal for well-formed 2dp input
steps: Call parse_money('1234.56')
Assert the result equals Decimal('1234.56') exactly
Assert the result type is Decimal and not float

description: parse_money rejects input with more than two decimal places instead of silently rounding
steps: Call parse_money('10.005') inside a pytest.raises(MoneyPrecisionError) block
Assert the exception is raised
Call parse_money('10.001') and assert MoneyPrecisionError is raised
Assert no rounded value such as Decimal('10.00') is ever returned for these inputs

description: quantize_money rounds half away from zero to two decimal places
steps: Assert quantize_money(Decimal('2.345')) == Decimal('2.35')
Assert quantize_money(Decimal('2.344')) == Decimal('2.34')
Assert quantize_money(Decimal('2.355')) == Decimal('2.36')
Assert the returned exponent is -2 for every case

description: Positive and non-negative money guards distinguish zero correctly
steps: Assert require_positive(Decimal('0.01')) does not raise
Assert require_positive(Decimal('0.00')) raises a DomainError subclass
Assert require_positive(Decimal('-1.00')) raises
Assert require_non_negative(Decimal('0.00')) does not raise while require_non_negative(Decimal('-0.01')) raises

description: format_money renders a fixed two-decimal string for whole and fractional amounts
steps: Assert format_money(Decimal('5')) == '5.00'
Assert format_money(Decimal('1234.5')) == '1234.50'
Assert format_money(Decimal('0')) == '0.00'

description: The money policy module contains no float construction or float type annotation
steps: Run: grep -nE 'float\(|:\s*float|%f' backend/src/domain/money.py
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Run: grep -nE '^(from|import) ' backend/src/domain/money.py
Assert every import line references only decimal, typing, or src.types

description: Money values round-trip through SQLite as Decimal with full precision preserved
steps: Create an in-memory SQLite table with a MoneyType column
Insert Decimal('1234.56') and commit
Read the row back and assert the value is exactly Decimal('1234.56')
Assert isinstance(value, Decimal) is True and isinstance(value, float) is False

description: MoneyType preserves trailing-zero scale for whole-currency amounts
steps: Insert Decimal('100.00') through a MoneyType column and read it back
Assert the returned value equals Decimal('100.00')
Assert str(value) == '100.00' so the two-decimal scale survives persistence

description: The session scope rolls back every write when an exception escapes the block
steps: Open a session scope and insert one account row without committing explicitly
Raise a RuntimeError inside the scope and catch it outside
Open a new session and count rows in the accounts table
Assert the count is 0

description: The session scope commits all writes when the block exits normally
steps: Open a session scope, insert one account row, and exit the block without error
Open a new session and query for the inserted row
Assert exactly one row is returned

description: Alembic upgrade head builds the full schema from an empty database
steps: Delete any existing SQLite database file
Run: cd backend && uv run alembic upgrade head
Assert the process exit code is 0
Query sqlite_master and assert tables customers, kyc_records, accounts, transactions, transfers, beneficiaries, loan_applications, loan_state_transitions, audit_entries and notifications all exist

description: No money column in the migrated schema is stored as REAL or FLOAT
steps: Run alembic upgrade head against a clean database
Query PRAGMA table_info(accounts) and locate the balance column
Assert its declared type starts with 'NUMERIC'
Query sqlite_master for all CREATE TABLE statements and assert none contains 'REAL' or 'FLOAT'

description: Repository layer contains no imports from Service or API layers
steps: Run: grep -rnE 'from (backend\.)?src\.(service|api)|import (backend\.)?src\.(service|api)' backend/src/repository/
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)

description: GET /health returns 200 with status ok and completes within one second
steps: Start the backend and wait for the startup event to complete
Record a monotonic timestamp, then issue GET /health
Assert the response status is 200 and the JSON body field 'status' equals 'ok'
Assert the elapsed wall-clock time for the request is under 1.0 second

description: The health check exercises a real database round-trip rather than returning a static literal
steps: Point the application at an unreachable or corrupt database URL
Issue GET /health
Assert the response status is not 200, proving the handler actually queries the database

description: Each request produces a parseable JSON log line carrying the four required keys
steps: Capture stdout while issuing GET /health
Parse each emitted line with json.loads and assert no line fails to parse
Assert at least one parsed record contains the keys timestamp, level, message and correlation_id
Assert the correlation_id value is a non-empty string

description: A supplied X-Correlation-ID propagates into both the response header and the log records
steps: Issue GET /health with header X-Correlation-ID: test-corr-123
Assert the response header X-Correlation-ID equals 'test-corr-123'
Assert at least one captured JSON log record has correlation_id == 'test-corr-123'

description: Absent a supplied header the middleware generates a distinct correlation ID per request
steps: Issue two sequential GET /health requests with no X-Correlation-ID header
Collect the correlation_id from each response header
Assert both values are non-empty and parse as UUIDs
Assert the two values are not equal

description: Passwords and bearer tokens are replaced with a redaction marker in emitted logs
steps: Log a structured record containing password='Hunter2!' and authorization='Bearer abc.def.ghi'
Capture the emitted log output as a string
Assert 'Hunter2!' does not appear anywhere in the output
Assert 'abc.def.ghi' does not appear and '***REDACTED***' does appear

description: KYC document numbers are redacted from log output
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/register then submit a KYC payload with document_number='X1234567'
Capture all log output produced during the request
Assert 'X1234567' does not appear in any emitted log line

description: A well-formed KYC document deterministically returns a VERIFIED verdict
steps: Call verify with document_type='PASSPORT' and document_number='P1234567'
Assert the returned verdict status is KycStatus.VERIFIED
Call verify twice more with identical input and assert the verdict is VERIFIED every time (determinism)

description: The reserved synthetic document number always returns REJECTED with a non-empty stub_reason
steps: Call verify with document_type='PASSPORT' and document_number='X0000000'
Assert the verdict status is KycStatus.REJECTED
Assert the verdict stub_reason is a non-empty string
Repeat the call three times and assert the result is REJECTED each time

description: Unrecognised document types and malformed document numbers raise a validation error
steps: Call verify with document_type='LIBRARY_CARD' inside pytest.raises and assert a validation error is raised
Call verify with document_type='PASSPORT' and document_number='!!' and assert a validation error is raised
Assert neither call returns a KycVerdict object

description: KYC verification does not gate on applicant age or date of birth
steps: Call verify with a well-formed document for an applicant whose date_of_birth is 16 years ago
Assert the verdict status is KycStatus.VERIFIED
Repeat with a date_of_birth 60 years ago and assert the verdict is also VERIFIED
Assert the verdict does not differ based on date_of_birth

description: No age or eligibility threshold function exists in the KYC policy module
steps: Run: grep -niE 'age|18|eligib|minor|adult' backend/src/domain/kyc_policy.py
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)

description: The KYC policy module is dependency-free and performs no I/O
steps: Run: grep -nE '^(from|import) ' backend/src/domain/kyc_policy.py
Assert every import references only datetime, typing, dataclasses, enum or src.types
Run: grep -nE 'open\(|requests\.|httpx\.|session|engine' backend/src/domain/kyc_policy.py and assert no matches
Run: cd backend && uv run mypy --strict src/domain/kyc_policy.py and assert exit code 0

description: A newly created customer defaults to PENDING_KYC status and CUSTOMER role
steps: Call create_customer with a unique email, password_hash, full_name and date_of_birth
Assert the returned record has a non-null id
Assert status == CustomerStatus.PENDING_KYC and role == Role.CUSTOMER
Re-read the row by id in a new session and assert the same status persists

description: Duplicate customer email insertion raises an integrity error and creates no second row
steps: Create a customer with email 'dup@horizon.test'
Attempt to create a second customer with the same email inside pytest.raises(IntegrityError)
Assert the error is raised
Query the customers table for that email and assert exactly one row exists

description: get_by_email returns None for an unknown address instead of raising
steps: Call get_by_email('nobody@horizon.test') against an empty table
Assert the return value is None and no exception is raised
Create a customer and call get_by_email with its address
Assert the returned record id matches the created customer

description: KYC records are created as PENDING and transition to VERIFIED with a timestamp
steps: Create a customer, then create a KYC record for that customer_id
Assert the record status is KycStatus.PENDING and verified_at is None
Call mark_verified on the record and re-read it
Assert status is VERIFIED and verified_at is a non-null datetime

description: A rejected KYC record stores the stub_reason supplied by the policy
steps: Create a PENDING KYC record and call mark_rejected with stub_reason='RESERVED_TEST_DOCUMENT'
Re-read the record in a new session
Assert status is KycStatus.REJECTED and stub_reason == 'RESERVED_TEST_DOCUMENT'

description: Registration stores a KDF hash rather than the plaintext password
steps: Call register with password 'Hunter2!Secure'
Read the persisted customer row
Assert password_hash != 'Hunter2!Secure' and len(password_hash) > 40
Assert the hash prefix identifies bcrypt or argon2 and that verifying 'Hunter2!Secure' against it returns True

description: Registering an email that already exists raises a duplicate error and creates no second customer
steps: Call register with email 'dup@horizon.test'
Call register again with the same email inside pytest.raises for the duplicate-email error
Assert the error is raised
Assert exactly one customer row exists for that email

description: A passing KYC submission activates the customer account
steps: Register a customer and assert status is PENDING_KYC
Call submit_kyc with document_type='PASSPORT' and document_number='P1234567'
Re-read the customer and assert status == CustomerStatus.ACTIVE
Assert the linked KYC record status is VERIFIED

description: A rejected KYC submission leaves the customer inactive
steps: Register a customer and call submit_kyc with document_number='X0000000'
Assert the KYC record status is REJECTED
Re-read the customer and assert status is still CustomerStatus.PENDING_KYC

description: A duplicate KYC submission raises KycAlreadySubmittedError and creates no second record
steps: Register a customer and complete a successful KYC submission
Call submit_kyc again for the same customer inside pytest.raises(KycAlreadySubmittedError)
Assert the error is raised
Count kyc_records rows for that customer_id and assert the count is 1

description: Successful login issues a JWT carrying subject, role and a 30-minute expiry
steps: Register and activate a customer, then call login with the correct password
Decode the returned token with the configured signing key
Assert the payload 'sub' matches the customer id and 'role' equals 'CUSTOMER'
Assert exp minus iat equals 1800 seconds

description: A wrong password raises an authentication error distinct from the not-activated error
steps: Register and activate a customer
Call login with an incorrect password inside pytest.raises for the authentication error
Assert the raised error type is the invalid-credentials error, not the not-activated error
Assert no token is returned

description: Login by a PENDING_KYC customer raises a distinct not-activated error
steps: Register a customer without submitting KYC
Call login with the correct password inside pytest.raises for the not-activated error
Assert the raised error is distinguishable from the invalid-credentials error by its error_code
Assert no token is returned

description: POST /api/v1/auth/register returns 201 with a customer id and PENDING_KYC status
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/register with a unique email, valid password, full_name and date_of_birth
Assert the response status is 201
Assert the JSON body contains a non-null 'id' and 'status' == 'PENDING_KYC'
Assert the response body contains no 'password' or 'password_hash' field

description: Registering a duplicate email returns 409
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/register with email 'dup@horizon.test' and assert 201
POST /api/v1/auth/register again with the same email
Assert the response status is 409

description: POST /api/v1/auth/kyc returns 200 and activates the customer on a passing verdict
steps: Register a customer, then POST /api/v1/auth/kyc with document_type='PASSPORT' and document_number='P1234567'
Assert the response status is 200 and the body status field is 'VERIFIED'
POST /api/v1/auth/login with that customer's credentials and assert status 200

description: Malformed KYC input returns 422 and a repeat submission returns 409
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/kyc with document_type='LIBRARY_CARD' and assert the response status is 422
Complete a valid KYC submission for a second customer and assert 200
POST /api/v1/auth/kyc again for that same customer and assert the response status is 409

description: Login returns 200 with a bearer access_token for an activated customer
steps: Register and complete KYC for a customer
POST /api/v1/auth/login with the correct email and password
Assert the response status is 200
Assert the body contains a non-empty 'access_token' and token_type == 'bearer'

description: Login returns 401 for bad credentials and 403 for an unactivated customer, with distinguishable responses
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/login with a correct email but wrong password and assert status 401
Register a new customer without KYC and POST /api/v1/auth/login with correct credentials
Assert the response status is 403
Assert the 403 body carries an error code identifying PENDING_KYC

description: GET /api/v1/auth/me returns the authenticated principal for a valid token
steps: Obtain an access_token via login
GET /api/v1/auth/me with header Authorization: Bearer <token>
Assert the response status is 200
Assert the body id, email and role match the logged-in customer

description: Missing, malformed and expired bearer tokens all return 401
steps: GET /api/v1/auth/me with no Authorization header and assert status 401
GET /api/v1/auth/me with header 'Authorization: Bearer not-a-jwt' and assert status 401
Mint a token with an exp in the past and GET /api/v1/auth/me with it
Assert the response status is 401

description: A CUSTOMER-role token calling an admin-guarded route receives 403
steps: Log in as a seeded CUSTOMER and obtain a token
Call an admin-guarded route with that token
Assert the response status is 403 and not 401 or 200

description: No public endpoint permits self-registration with the ADMIN role
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/register with an extra field role='ADMIN'
Assert the response is 201 or 422 but never creates an admin
Read the created customer row and assert role == 'CUSTOMER'
Run: grep -rn "Role.ADMIN" backend/src/api/routes/auth.py and assert no assignment of ADMIN occurs in a registration handler

description: audit_repository.append persists one entry with a server-assigned occurred_at timestamp
steps: Call append with actor_id, actor_role='CUSTOMER', action='TRANSFER_COMPLETED', entity_type='Transfer', entity_id and a correlation_id
Assert the returned row has a non-null id and a non-null occurred_at
Query audit_entries and assert exactly one row exists with action == 'TRANSFER_COMPLETED'

description: The audit repository public surface contains no update or delete method
steps: Introspect the AuditRepository class with dir()
Filter to public callables not starting with an underscore
Assert no name contains 'update', 'delete', 'remove' or 'purge'
Run: grep -niE 'def .*(update|delete)' backend/src/repository/audit_repository.py and assert no matches

description: A raw UPDATE against audit_entries is rejected by a database trigger
steps: Append one audit entry and record its action value
Execute raw SQL: UPDATE audit_entries SET action='tampered' inside pytest.raises for a database error
Assert the error is raised
Re-read the row and assert its action still holds the original value

description: A raw DELETE against audit_entries is rejected by a database trigger
steps: Append two audit entries and assert the row count is 2
Execute raw SQL: DELETE FROM audit_entries inside pytest.raises for a database error
Assert the error is raised
Re-count audit_entries and assert the count is still 2

description: Audit queries filter by entity_type and return most-recent-first ordering
steps: Append three entries with entity_type values 'Transfer', 'LoanApplication' and 'Transfer'
Query with entity_type='Transfer' and assert exactly 2 rows are returned
Assert the returned rows are ordered with the newest occurred_at first

description: Audit queries filter by actor_id and by an occurred_at date range
steps: Append entries for two distinct actor_id values
Query filtered by the first actor_id and assert only that actor's entries are returned
Query with a date range that excludes all entries and assert an empty list is returned

description: A failed audit append rolls back the enclosing business transaction
steps: Open a transaction, write a business row, then force the audit append to raise
Allow the exception to propagate out of the transaction scope
Open a new session and assert the business row was not committed
Assert the audit_entries table contains no partial entry for the operation

description: A created savings account starts at exactly Decimal 0.00 with ACTIVE status
steps: Call create_account for an existing customer_id
Assert the returned account balance == Decimal('0.00') and its type is SAVINGS
Assert status == AccountStatus.ACTIVE and account_number is a non-empty string
Re-read the row in a new session and assert the balance is still Decimal('0.00')

description: Generated account numbers are unique across accounts
steps: Create three accounts for the same customer
Collect the three account_number values
Assert all three are distinct
Attempt to insert a duplicate account_number directly and assert an integrity error is raised

description: get_for_update re-reads the current committed balance inside the transaction
steps: Create an account and set its balance to Decimal('100.00')
In transaction one, debit 40.00 and commit
In a new transaction, call get_for_update on the same account id
Assert the returned balance is Decimal('60.00')

description: A single transfer id yields exactly one DEBIT and one CREDIT transaction row
steps: Record a DEBIT row and a CREDIT row sharing transfer_id T1
Query transactions filtered by transfer_id == T1
Assert exactly 2 rows are returned
Assert one row has direction DEBIT and the other CREDIT, and their amounts are equal

description: Each transaction row stores the resulting balance_after as a Decimal
steps: Record a DEBIT of 25.00 against an account whose balance becomes 75.00
Read the transaction row back
Assert balance_after == Decimal('75.00') and isinstance(balance_after, Decimal)

description: Statement listing paginates most-recent-first with a correct total count
steps: Record 25 transactions against one account with increasing created_at values
Call list_statements with page=1 and page_size=20
Assert 20 items are returned, the total count is 25, and the first item is the newest
Call with page=2 and assert exactly 5 items are returned

description: An account with no transactions returns an empty page rather than raising
steps: Create an account and record no transactions
Call list_statements with page=1
Assert the returned item list is empty and total is 0
Assert no exception is raised

description: Opening an account creates a zero-balance savings account and one matching audit entry
steps: Call open_account for an authenticated customer principal
Assert the returned account balance == Decimal('0.00')
Query audit_entries for entity_type='Account' and entity_id equal to the new account id
Assert exactly one entry exists with action == 'ACCOUNT_OPENED' and actor_id equal to the customer id

description: Account listing is scoped to the calling principal only
steps: Create customer A with two accounts and customer B with one account
Call list_accounts for principal A
Assert exactly 2 accounts are returned and every id belongs to A
Assert customer B's account id does not appear in the result

description: Requesting another customer's statements raises an ownership error
steps: Create customer A with an account and customer B
Call get_statements with principal B and customer A's account_id inside pytest.raises(OwnershipError)
Assert the error is raised
Assert no statement rows are returned to B

description: The account service returns Decimal balances and contains no float usage
steps: Call list_accounts and inspect the balance on each returned account
Assert isinstance(balance, Decimal) for every account
Run: grep -nE 'float\(|:\s*float' backend/src/service/account_service.py
Assert the command exits with status 1

description: Statement page size is read from configuration and applied to service results
steps: Record 30 transactions on an owned account
Call get_statements with no explicit page size and assert 20 items are returned
Override statement_page_size to 5 in configuration and repeat the call
Assert exactly 5 items are returned, proving the value is configuration-driven

description: POST /api/v1/accounts returns 201 with a zero balance rendered as the string 0.00
steps: Authenticate as a customer and POST /api/v1/accounts
Assert the response status is 201
Assert the raw response text contains '"balance":"0.00"' or '"balance": "0.00"'
Assert json.loads gives balance as a str instance, not a float

description: POST /api/v1/accounts without a bearer token returns 401
steps: POST /api/v1/accounts with no Authorization header
Assert the response status is 401
Assert no account row was created in the database

description: GET /api/v1/accounts returns 200 listing only the caller's own accounts
steps: Create two accounts as customer A and one as customer B
GET /api/v1/accounts authenticated as A
Assert the response status is 200 and the array length is 2
Assert no returned account id belongs to customer B

description: The statements endpoint returns a paginated envelope with items, page, page_size and total
steps: Seed 25 transactions on an owned account
GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}/statements?page=1
Assert the response status is 200 and the body has keys items, page, page_size and total
Assert len(items) == 20 and total == 25

description: An account with no transactions returns 200 with an empty items array rather than 404
steps: Create a fresh account with no transactions
GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}/statements
Assert the response status is 200 and not 404
Assert items is an empty array and total is 0

description: Cross-customer statement access returns 403
steps: Create an account as customer A and authenticate as customer B
GET /api/v1/accounts/{A_account_id}/statements as B
Assert the response status is exactly 403
Assert the response body contains no transaction data

description: Zero and negative transfer amounts are rejected by the policy
steps: Evaluate the transfer policy with amount=Decimal('0.00') and assert a DomainError subclass is raised
Evaluate with amount=Decimal('-5.00') and assert a DomainError subclass is raised
Assert neither call returns an allow decision

description: An amount with more than two decimal places is rejected rather than silently rounded
steps: Evaluate the transfer policy with amount=Decimal('10.001')
Assert a MoneyPrecisionError or DomainError subclass is raised
Assert the policy does not return an allow decision carrying a rounded 10.00 amount

description: A self-transfer is rejected with an error code distinct from insufficient funds
steps: Evaluate the policy with source_account_id equal to destination_account_id
Assert a DomainError subclass identifying a self-transfer is raised
Assert the error_code is distinct from 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS'

description: A closed or non-existent destination account is rejected
steps: Evaluate the policy with a destination account whose status is AccountStatus.CLOSED and assert a DomainError subclass is raised
Evaluate the policy with a destination account that does not exist and assert a DomainError subclass is raised
Evaluate the same case with an existing ACTIVE destination and assert no error is raised

description: An amount above the balance raises InsufficientFundsException
steps: Evaluate the policy with balance=Decimal('100.00') and amount=Decimal('100.01')
Assert InsufficientFundsException is raised
Assert the exception error_code equals 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS'

description: A transfer of exactly the full available balance is permitted with no minimum-balance floor
steps: Evaluate the policy with balance=Decimal('100.00') and amount=Decimal('100.00')
Assert no exception is raised and the policy returns an allow decision
Assert no minimum-balance rule blocks draining the account to 0.00

description: A transfer to a valid active non-beneficiary account is permitted by the policy
steps: Evaluate the policy with a valid ACTIVE destination account that the sender has not saved as a beneficiary
Assert no exception is raised
Assert the policy returns an allow decision

description: The transfer policy module contains no beneficiary check
steps: Run: grep -niE 'beneficiar' backend/src/domain/transfer_policy.py
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Inspect the policy function signature and assert it accepts no beneficiary parameter

description: A large transfer within balance is permitted with no cap applied
steps: Evaluate the policy with balance=Decimal('1000000.00') and amount=Decimal('999999.99')
Assert no exception is raised and the policy returns an allow decision
Assert no cap-exceeded error type exists in the raised-error surface

description: No cap, limit or velocity threshold appears in the transfer policy module
steps: Run: grep -niE 'cap|daily|velocity|limit' backend/src/domain/transfer_policy.py
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Inspect the policy function signature and assert it accepts no daily_cap or limit parameter

description: Adding a beneficiary persists the record and writes a matching audit entry
steps: Call add_beneficiary as customer A with nickname='Mum' and a valid destination account_number
Assert the returned record has a non-null id and deleted_at is None
Query audit_entries for entity_type='Beneficiary' and the new id
Assert exactly one entry exists with action == 'BENEFICIARY_ADDED' and actor_id equal to customer A

description: Beneficiary listing is scoped to the owning customer
steps: Add one beneficiary as customer A and one as customer B
Call list_beneficiaries as B
Assert exactly one record is returned and it is B's
Assert A's beneficiary id does not appear in B's result

description: Removing a beneficiary sets deleted_at and hides it from listings without deleting the row
steps: Add a beneficiary as customer A and call remove_beneficiary on it
Call list_beneficiaries for A and assert the removed beneficiary is absent
Query the beneficiaries table directly by id and assert the row still exists

Assert the status DISBURSED is rendered
Assert the formatted principal '5,000.00' is displayed as the disbursed amount

description: A customer with no loans sees an empty state with an apply action
steps: Render the Loans screen with the loans endpoint mocked to return an empty array
Assert an empty-state message is rendered
Assert a visible control to start a loan application is present

description: The loan queue renders applications with their key fields
steps: Render the LoanQueue with the admin loans endpoint mocked to return three applications
Assert three queue rows are rendered
Assert each row displays applicant, formatted principal, tenure and status

description: Selecting a status filter re-queries the admin loans endpoint
steps: Render the LoanQueue and select the UNDER_REVIEW status filter
Assert GET /api/v1/admin/loans was called with status=UNDER_REVIEW
Assert the rendered rows update to the filtered payload

description: Approving with an empty reason is blocked before any API call
steps: Open the approve action on an UNDER_REVIEW loan and leave the reason field empty
Attempt to submit the decision
Assert no POST to the approve endpoint was made
Assert a validation message or disabled submit control prevents the action

description: Rejecting with a whitespace-only reason is blocked before any API call
steps: Open the reject action and enter only spaces in the reason field
Attempt to submit the decision
Assert no POST to the reject endpoint was made
Assert a validation message is rendered

description: A valid approval calls the approve endpoint and updates the row status
steps: Open the approve action on an UNDER_REVIEW loan and enter reason 'Documents verified'
Submit with the endpoint mocked to return 200 and status APPROVED
Assert POST /api/v1/admin/loans/{id}/approve was called with that reason
Assert the row status updates to APPROVED without a page reload

description: A valid rejection calls the reject endpoint and updates the row status
steps: Open the reject action and enter reason 'Insufficient documentation'
Submit with the endpoint mocked to return 200 and status REJECTED
Assert POST /api/v1/admin/loans/{id}/reject was called with that reason
Assert the row status updates to REJECTED

description: Actions are offered only where the transition is legal for the row's status
steps: Render the queue with loans in APPLIED, UNDER_REVIEW and APPROVED states
Assert the APPLIED row offers review but not approve or disburse
Assert the UNDER_REVIEW row offers approve and reject but not disburse
Assert the APPROVED row offers disburse

description: A 409 response renders an explicit illegal-transition message
steps: Trigger a decision action with the endpoint mocked to return 409
Assert an error message referring to an invalid state transition is rendered
Assert the row status is not optimistically changed

description: The audit viewer renders all required columns for each ledger entry
steps: Render the AuditLog with the endpoint mocked to return entries for a Transfer and a LoanApplication
Assert both entries are rendered as rows
Assert each row displays timestamp, actor, action, entity type and entity reference

description: Audit filters re-query the endpoint with the chosen entity type and date range
steps: Render the AuditLog and select entity type 'Transfer'
Assert GET /api/v1/admin/audit was called with entity_type=Transfer
Apply a date range filter and assert the endpoint was called with the from and to values
Assert the rendered rows update to the filtered payload

description: The audit viewer exposes no edit or delete affordance
steps: Render the AuditLog with several entries
Assert no button or link with an edit, delete or remove accessible name is present
Run: grep -niE 'delete|put|patch|post' frontend/src/pages/admin/AuditLog.tsx
Assert no mutating API call against the audit resource is found

description: The notification viewer renders channel, event type and status for each entry
steps: Render the Notifications screen with the endpoint mocked to return a transfer event and a loan transition event
Assert both entries are rendered as rows
Assert each row displays channel, event_type and status

description: Notification delivery status values are visually distinguishable
steps: Render the Notifications screen with entries in QUEUED, SENT and FAILED status
Assert all three rows render
Assert the FAILED entry is rendered with a distinct status treatment from SENT
Assert the status is conveyed by text and not by colour alone

description: Customer screens render without horizontal overflow at mobile and tablet widths
steps: Load each customer screen in Playwright at a 375px viewport
Assert document.scrollWidth is not greater than the 375px viewport width on each
Repeat at a 768px viewport and assert no horizontal overflow on each screen

description: Admin tabular screens remain usable at the desktop breakpoint
steps: Load the admin loan queue and audit log at a 1440px viewport
Assert all table column headers are visible without horizontal scrolling
Assert row action controls are reachable and not clipped

description: Axe reports zero serious or critical violations across all screens
steps: Run an axe scan against each of the eleven screens at a 375px viewport
Assert the count of violations with impact 'serious' or 'critical' is 0 for each
Repeat the scan at a 1440px viewport and assert the same
Write the axe results to a committed artefact for evidence

description: The transfer flow can be completed end to end using only the keyboard
steps: Load the Transfer screen in Playwright and navigate using Tab and Enter only
Complete destination entry, amount entry and confirmation without using the mouse
Assert the success state is reached
Assert every focused element shows a visible focus indicator distinguishable from its unfocused state

description: The loan review flow including the reason field is keyboard operable
steps: Load the admin LoanQueue and navigate to a loan's approve action using the keyboard only
Enter a reason and submit using the keyboard only
Assert the decision is submitted successfully
Assert focus is moved to the resulting status message

description: Each screen exposes semantic landmarks and exactly one h1
steps: Load each screen and query for main, nav and header landmark roles
Assert a main landmark is present on every screen
Assert exactly one h1 element exists per screen

description: All rendered money values meet AA contrast against their background
steps: Load the Dashboard, AccountDetail and Transfer screens
Compute the computed-style contrast ratio for each rendered money element against its background
Assert every ratio is at least 4.5:1

description: At least three architecture structural tests exist and pass in the default test run
steps: Count test functions under tests/architecture/ and assert the count is at least 3
Run the default backend test command
Assert the architecture tests are collected and all pass
Assert the process exit code is 0

description: The import-linter contract passes against the clean codebase
steps: Run: cd backend && uv run lint-imports
Assert the process exit code is 0
Assert the output reports the layered contract as kept

description: An injected upward import is detected and fails the contract
steps: Temporarily add an import of src.api into a module under src/repository/
Run: cd backend && uv run lint-imports
Assert the process exit code is non-zero and the violation is named in the output
Revert the temporary import and assert the contract passes again

description: No API route module imports a repository module directly
steps: Run: grep -rnE 'from (backend\.)?src\.repository|import (backend\.)?src\.repository' backend/src/api/routes/
Assert the command exits with status 1 (no matches)
Assert the equivalent structural test in tests/architecture/ passes

description: The domain policy package has no dependency outside the standard library and types
steps: Parse the import statements of every module under backend/src/domain/
Assert no import references src.config, src.repository, src.service or src.api
Assert no third-party package is imported by any domain module
Assert the corresponding structural test passes

description: Dependency-cruiser reports zero frontend boundary violations
steps: Run the dependency-cruiser validation command in the frontend workspace
Assert the process exit code is 0
Assert the reported error count is 0

description: The money-precision hook blocks a write introducing float into a money path
steps: Invoke the hook with a candidate write containing 'balance: float = 0.0'
Assert the hook exits with a blocking status and emits a message naming the money precision rule
Invoke the hook with the equivalent 'balance: Decimal' write
Assert the hook permits the write

description: The audit-immutability hook blocks writes that mutate the audit table
steps: Invoke the hook with a candidate write containing 'DELETE FROM audit_entries'
Assert the hook exits with a blocking status
Invoke the hook with a write containing an ORM update against the AuditEntry model and assert it is blocked
Invoke the hook with an audit append call and assert it is permitted

description: The pii-scrub hook blocks writes that log credentials or document numbers
steps: Invoke the hook with a candidate write containing logger.info with a password variable interpolated
Assert the hook exits with a blocking status
Invoke the hook with a write logging a document_number field and assert it is blocked
Invoke the hook with a write logging only a correlation_id and assert it is permitted

description: At least two banking-specific skills exist beyond the Harness defaults
steps: List the directories under .claude/skills/ and identify those added for the banking domain
Assert at least 2 banking-specific skills are present
Assert each has a SKILL.md with a valid name and description front matter

description: At least two banking-specific commands exist beyond scaffold.md
steps: List the files under .claude/commands/
Assert the count is at least 3 including the pre-existing scaffold.md
Assert at least 2 files are banking-domain commands
Assert each command file carries a valid description front matter

description: At least two banking-specific agent definitions exist with valid front matter
steps: List the files under .claude/agents/ and identify those added for the banking domain
Assert at least 2 banking-specific agents are present beyond the seven Harness defaults
Assert each declares a name, a description and a tools list
Assert each agent file parses as valid front matter plus body

description: init.sh brings the full stack up from a clean checkout
steps: From a clean checkout with no database file, run ./init.sh
Poll http://localhost:8000/health with 5 retries at 2s backoff
Assert a 200 response with status 'ok' is received
Assert the frontend root at http://localhost:3000 returns a 200 response

description: The seed script is idempotent and can be re-run without duplicating data
steps: Run the seed script twice against the same database
Assert the second run exits with status 0
Assert the customer count is the same after both runs
Assert exactly one admin customer exists

description: Seeded data covers funded customers, a beneficiary and loans in each reviewable state
steps: Run the seed script against a clean database
Assert at least 2 customers exist with role CUSTOMER and at least one account each with a balance above 0.00
Assert at least one beneficiary row exists
Assert at least one loan exists in each of APPLIED, UNDER_REVIEW and APPROVED status

description: Exactly one administrator exists and is created only by the seed script
steps: Run the seed script and query customers with role ADMIN
Assert exactly one admin row exists
Run: grep -rn 'Role.ADMIN' backend/src/api/ and assert no route assigns the ADMIN role

description: All seeded records use reserved synthetic identifiers
steps: Read every seeded customer email address
Assert each uses a reserved test domain such as .test or example.com
Assert no seeded document number matches a real-world identifier format in production use
Run the detect-secrets hook against the seed script and assert it reports no findings

description: The README quick-start covers prerequisites, the run command and seeded credentials
steps: Assert README.md exists and contains a quick-start section
Assert it names the prerequisite runtimes and the ./init.sh command
Assert it documents the seeded administrator login and the API and UI URLs
Assert it states that all data is synthetic

description: The GitLab CI configuration is valid and defines build and test stages for both workspaces
steps: Assert .gitlab-ci.yml exists at the repository root
Parse the file with a YAML parser and assert it loads without error
Assert the stages list includes a build stage and a test stage
Assert jobs exist that run the backend pytest suite and the frontend vitest suite

description: No GitHub Actions workflow is used as the graded CI artefact
steps: Assert .gitlab-ci.yml is present and non-empty
Assert the CI test job references the architecture structural tests
Assert the pipeline does not depend on .github/workflows to run the graded checks

description: The coverage gate blocks the pipeline below the 80% floor
steps: Run the backend test job with the coverage threshold configured at 80
Assert pytest is invoked with a fail-under setting of 80
Simulate a run whose coverage is below 80 and assert the job exits non-zero
Assert the committed coverage artefact exists after a passing run

description: The Claude Code Action job reads credentials from CI variables and commits no secret
steps: Assert .gitlab-ci.yml defines a job invoking the Claude Code Action or equivalent
Assert the job references an API key through a CI variable reference
Run: grep -nE 'sk-ant|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\s*[:=]\s*[A-Za-z0-9]' .gitlab-ci.yml
Assert the command returns no match

description: Lint and typecheck gates run for both workspaces and fail the pipeline on error
steps: Assert the pipeline defines jobs running ruff check and mypy for the backend
Assert it defines jobs running eslint and tsc for the frontend
Introduce a deliberate type error and run the typecheck job
Assert the job exits non-zero, then revert and assert it passes

description: The root .mcp.json declares a Playwright MCP server and parses as valid JSON
steps: Assert .mcp.json exists at the repository root
Parse it with json.loads and assert it loads without error
Assert it contains an mcpServers entry naming a Playwright server
Assert the entry declares a runnable command

description: An evaluator run produces a committed artefact evidencing Playwright MCP invocation
steps: Run the evaluator against the running application
Assert an artefact is written under specs/reviews/ for that run
Assert the artefact records the Playwright MCP driven UI verification steps and their pass or fail outcome
Assert the artefact references at least one screen verified through MCP rather than through direct HTTP calls

description: The E2E suite covers every acceptance criterion journey and passes
steps: Run the Playwright suite against the seeded running system
Assert the process exit code is 0
Assert at least one spec exists referencing each of AC-01 through AC-10 by identifier
Assert the onboarding, transfer, loan application and admin review journeys each have a passing spec

description: An end-to-end transfer journey asserts money conservation in the browser
steps: Log in as a seeded funded customer and record the displayed balances of both accounts
Complete a transfer through the UI
Assert the source balance decreased and the destination increased by exactly the transferred amount
Assert the sum of the two displayed balances is unchanged

description: Snapshots are committed for all three breakpoints and are stable across runs
steps: Run the Playwright suite with snapshot capture enabled
Assert a committed snapshot directory exists containing images for the 375px, 768px and 1440px viewports
Re-run the suite against unchanged UI
Assert no snapshot comparison failure is reported

description: A script under scripts/ imports and invokes the Claude Agent SDK programmatically
steps: List Python files under scripts/ and assert at least one exists
Run: grep -rnE 'claude_agent_sdk|claude_code_sdk' scripts/ and assert at least one import match
Assert the script calls an SDK entry point such as a query or client invocation
Assert the file is not merely a slash command definition or an agent markdown file

description: The SDK script is executable and exits cleanly in a dry-run mode
steps: Run the script with a dry-run or help flag
Assert the process exits with status 0
Assert it prints a usage or plan summary rather than raising an import error

description: The SDK script performs a real repository task and writes an output artefact
steps: Run the script against the repository
Assert it exits with status 0
Assert it writes an output artefact to a documented path
Assert the artefact content reflects actual repository state rather than static placeholder text

description: The SDK script contains no committed credential
steps: Run: grep -nE 'sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9]' scripts/ and assert no match
Assert the script reads its key from an environment variable
Run the detect-secrets hook against scripts/ and assert it reports no findings

description: The Agent SDK is a declared dependency rather than an ambient install
steps: Locate the dependency manifest covering scripts/
Assert the Claude Agent SDK package is listed as a dependency
Assert a lockfile entry exists for it
Install from the manifest in a clean environment and assert the script imports successfully

description: The root plugin.json exists, parses, and identifies the banking substrate
steps: Assert plugin.json exists at the repository root
Parse it with json.loads and assert it loads without error
Assert it declares name, version and description fields
Assert the description identifies the ClaudeForge banking substrate rather than the generic Harness

description: The root and Harness plugin manifests both exist and differ in content
steps: Assert both plugin.json and .claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json exist
Compute a hash of each file's contents
Assert the two hashes differ
Assert the root manifest declares a different name from the Harness manifest

description: Every substrate path referenced by the root plugin manifest resolves to an existing file
steps: Parse plugin.json and collect every referenced agent, skill, command and hook path
Assert the manifest references at least 2 agents, 2 skills, 2 commands and 1 hook
Assert every referenced path exists on disk
Assert no referenced path points outside the repository

description: specs/app_spec.md states all ten ACs and all eight NFRs
steps: Assert specs/app_spec.md exists
Assert it contains an identifier for each of AC-01 through AC-10
Assert it contains an identifier for each of NFR-01 through NFR-08
Assert each identifier is accompanied by a full requirement statement rather than a bare reference

description: CLAUDE.md references app_spec.md instead of restating the requirement text
steps: Read CLAUDE.md and assert it contains a reference to specs/app_spec.md as the authoritative requirement source
Assert CLAUDE.md no longer contains the full inline NFR-01 through NFR-08 statement table
Assert the Spec-Is-Truth rule remains stated in CLAUDE.md

description: No requirement identifier is defined in two places with differing text
steps: Extract every AC-NN and NFR-NN statement from specs/app_spec.md
Extract any AC-NN or NFR-NN statement remaining in CLAUDE.md
Assert no identifier carries a substantive requirement statement in both files
Assert the two documents do not contradict each other

description: Every acceptance criterion traces to a story and a feature
steps: Parse the AC identifiers from specs/app_spec.md
Grep specs/stories/ for each identifier and assert every AC appears in at least one story file
Parse specs/features.json and assert every AC identifier appears in at least one feature description or step
Assert no AC identifier is unreferenced

description: The authoritative spec contains no invented business rule
steps: Run: grep -niE 'daily cap|transfer cap|velocity|minimum balance|eligibility threshold|minimum age' specs/app_spec.md
Assert the command returns no match asserting such a rule as a requirement
Assert any mention of these appears only as an explicit statement that no such rule exists
Assert every requirement in the file cites an AC-NN or NFR-NN identifier

description: The architecture document contains a diagram covering all six layers
steps: Assert docs/architecture.md exists
Assert it contains a diagram block such as a mermaid graph or an embedded image reference
Assert the diagram names all six layers Types, Config, Repository, Service, API and UI
Assert the audit and notification modules are shown as cross-cutting

description: The TDD document includes a concrete red-then-green worked example
steps: Assert docs/tdd.md exists
Assert it contains a worked example naming a specific test and the implementation that followed
Assert it shows the failing state preceding the passing state
Assert it references the 80% coverage floor and the 100% target

description: A recorded fix loop documents the full detect-to-PR trace
steps: Assert at least one file exists under docs/fix-loops/
Assert it documents distinct detect, reproduce, fix and validate phases
Assert it references a real failing test or evaluator finding by identifier
Assert it links to the branch or merge that resolved it

description: Knowledge deposits are recorded and cross-referenced to learned rules
steps: Assert docs/knowledge-deposits.md exists and contains at least one dated entry
Assert each entry states a reusable lesson rather than a task log line
Assert it cross-references .claude/state/learned-rules.md

description: At least two sprint cycles are evidenced by contracts and evaluator outputs
steps: List files under sprint-contracts/ and assert at least 2 sprint contracts exist
List files under specs/reviews/ and assert at least 2 evaluator outputs exist
Assert the outputs are from distinct iterations showing a ratcheting improvement in score or pass count
